decisions.decision: Build the choices from ScrapTypeCatalog.All in its own order, then append arrangement-only types
decisions.why: FR-002 names the shared list and forbids a second one, and the arrangement exposes its types alphabetised
decisions.rejected: using LuggerArrangementSnapshot.ScrapTypes alone, which would reorder the plant list and vanish when the arrangement cannot be read

decisions.decision: Filter both sources through ScrapDecisionRules before they reach the options
decisions.why: the arrangement holds whatever an operator typed, so an entry spelled No Scrap would otherwise be offered
decisions.rejected: trusting the catalog to be the only source

decisions.decision: Resolve the card's lugger from a snapshot read once per list load, through LuggerArrangementSnapshot.Resolve
decisions.why: Resolve is the rule set the work-order card already uses, so the two cannot disagree (FR-007)
decisions.rejected: copying the rule set into the board, or reusing the work-order availability provider, which answers per work centre from the active job

decisions.decision: Tell the three card outcomes apart by the snapshot's row count
decisions.why: an empty snapshot and an unassigned type both report NotConfigured, so only the row count separates an outage from a gap
decisions.rejected: dropping the lugger cell when the arrangement cannot be read, as the work-order card does, because FR-010 requires the type to still be named

decisions.decision: Store the stated type on answers_json under the key scrap.type and never store the lugger
decisions.why: A2 keeps the type and makes the dump point a live fact, and the answers column needs no schema change
decisions.rejected: a new column and procedure pair, or storing the resolved lugger beside the type

decisions.why: an arrangement that could not be read yields no count, and drawing a confident zero would be a lie
decisions.rejected: showing zero for every type when the read failed

decisions.decision: A generic card draws no lugger artwork
decisions.why: the job's artwork belongs to the job and this chunk asks only for the name; borrowing it would show another job's lugger
decisions.rejected: resolving lugger pictures through a second resolver for generic cards

decisions.decision: The stated scrap type is cleared when the work center changes
decisions.why: a type stated for one work center says nothing about another
decisions.rejected: carrying it, which would raise a request nobody described

decisions.decision: The stated scrap type outranks the work center's job scrap type on the card line
decisions.why: a card that named the job's type while its own cell named the requester's would show two types, which is the disagreement FR-007 exists to prevent

decisions.decision: A generic scrap card never borrows the job's lugger artwork
decisions.why: that picture belongs to the job's scrap type, so it would send a handler to a lugger the card does not name
decisions.rejected: gating only the cell and leaving the card's left spot

decisions.decision: A scrap choice is the type's name and nothing else
decisions.why: owner direction: the lugger count is a capacity fact the requester never acts on, and the lugger they walk to is the waitlist card's to name
decisions.rejected: keeping the count but hiding the column

decisions.decision: The stated scrap type became the request's stored detail
decisions.why: the queue refuses a second active request when building, work center, item and detail all match, so an empty detail made every scrap request at a work center a duplicate of the first
decisions.rejected: relaxing the duplicate rule itself, which is correct for a genuine double-tap

decisions.decision: The review shows the queue's own refusal sentence
decisions.why: the review read perfectly well and only the raise failed, so 'this step could not be read' told the requester nothing they could act on
decisions.rejected: leaving the frame's generic unavailable text

decisions.decision: The stage row is drawn only for a request type that derives one
decisions.why: a stage comes from a proved part's operation state, so a scrap, dunnage or die request was reporting 'Not recorded' about something it never had
decisions.rejected: hiding the row only when its value is blank, which would keep the row for every non-part request

decisions.decision: The generic result page is a copy of NewRequestResultPage: glyph, heading, sentence, progress ring, and the same buttons per outcome (Add Another Request + Return to Waitlist on success, Return to Waitlist on a duplicate, Close + Retry on a failure).
A queue refusal now travels as GenericRequestSubmission.IsDuplicate and GenericRequestDraft.ResultWasDuplicate, so the result step can draw it as its own outcome rather than as a fault.
Retry on the result page resubmits through the data seam instead of rebinding the inherited reload command, which would only redraw the same failure.
Duplicates still stop on the review step, as FR-018 says; the result page's duplicate outcome covers a retry that the queue refuses.

concerns.note: Five tests in MTM_Waitlist.Tests/Module_Mock_Service/RunHistoryStoreTests fail before and after this change: they hardcode a 2026-09-12 cycle instant while RunHistoryStore prunes records older than HistoryRetentionDays (60 days) against the real clock, so those records are deleted as they are written. They crossed the boundary on 2026-11-11. Not caused by this feature and not fixed here.

Resolved after the run: RunHistoryStoreTests now derives every instant from a per-test clock and always hands that clock to the store. The earlier five failures were hardcoded 2026-09-12 records pruned by a 60-day retention window measured against the real clock.

Owner direction on 2026-11-13 added FR-015 to FR-018 after this spec shipped. They are implemented and tested, and recorded here rather than as tasks.md boxes because the writer refuses to append tasks to a shipped spec.

The same duplicate collision can affect a generic PART request (chunk 017), whose stored detail is also empty because the part step answers through its own seam. Not changed here: doing so would alter 017's stored shape and card semantics without a verified need.
